items.title: CSM cast list omits volumetric casters (Voxel, GaussianSplat)
items.claim: Only Model + Globe set _shadowCastLayout; collections are non-goals; volumetric casters need deep-shadow techniques, filed as NEW-CSM-VOLUMETRIC-CASTERS.
items.evidence: `_shadowCastLayout` is set only in WebGPUCSMCastPass.ts, WebGPUCSMRenderer.ts, WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts, WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts, WebGPUModelRenderer.ts, WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.ts, WebGPUPrimitiveShadowCast.ts, WebGPUShadowMapRenderer.js — no voxel or splat renderer. The id is cited by NEXT_QUEUE_2026-07-04.md:101 (demand-gated) and ISSUES_AND_FIXED_BUGS.md:188 (OPEN by design) but is DEFINED nowhere: DEFERRED_WORK.md has no NEW-CSM-VOLUMETRIC-CASTERS entry, and QUEUE_2026-08-09_CAMPAIGN18.md has no voxel/splat shadow-casting row.
items.surviving_record: NEXT_QUEUE_2026-07-04.md:101 and ISSUES_AND_FIXED_BUGS.md:188 reference the id; no defining row exists
items.migrate_text: WebGPU cascaded shadow maps take casters only from renderers that set `_shadowCastLayout`: models (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts), globe tiles (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts / WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts) and geometry primitives (WebGPUPrimitiveCommands.ts / WebGPUPrimitiveShadowCast.ts). Voxel volumes (WebGPUVoxelRenderer.ts) and Gaussian splats (WebGPUGaussianSplatRenderer.ts) cast no shadow; upstream WebGL does not cast from them either, and screen-space collections (billboard, label, point, polyline) are deliberate non-goals on both backends. Casting from volumetric content needs a deep-shadow-map or transmittance-accumulation technique rather than a cast-layout registration, so this stays demand-gated as NEW-CSM-VOLUMETRIC-CASTERS; the id must be given a defining row (DEFERRED_WORK.md or the C18 queue) because today it is only referenced.

items.title: §2a hotspot 2 / §4 hotspot 2 / rec: JSON.stringify-keyed sampler and BGL caches in WebGPUContext.ts
items.claim: `getOrCreateSampler` / `getOrCreateBindGroupLayout` key on `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`; allocation per lookup, hot during pipeline builds; replace with a structural hash.
items.evidence: WebGPUContext.ts:5595-5608 `getOrCreateSampler` — `const key = JSON.stringify(descriptor)` at :5599; :5615-5628 `getOrCreateBindGroupLayout` — `JSON.stringify(descriptor)` at :5622. No DEFERRED_WORK, FIX_QUEUE, FAR or DX row names these two caches (the only related landing is the pipeline-cache key hand-serialization, DEFERRED_WORK.md:12782-12791, which explicitly scopes to `generateCacheKey`).
items.migrate_text: `WebGPUContext.getOrCreateSampler` (packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:5599) and `getOrCreateBindGroupLayout` (:5622) still key their caches on `JSON.stringify(descriptor)`, so every lookup walks the descriptor and allocates a string, and key equality is sensitive to property order. The pipeline cache dropped `JSON.stringify` for its primitive/blend segments (WebGPURenderPipelineCache.ts:940-943, :1065) with an explicit rationale that a descriptor memo would go stale for producers that mutate descriptors in place (DEFERRED_WORK.md:12788-12791); the sampler/BGL caches never received the same treatment. Cost is small per call but sits on every pipeline build and bind-group-layout resolution; a hand-serialized key over the few fields each descriptor carries is the fix. No row owns it.

items.migrate_text: `WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.configure` (packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:606-625) still allocates both full-resolution ping and pong intermediates in `_intermediateFormat` (rgba16float under HDR) regardless of stage count, while `execute` (:1504-1512) bypasses them entirely through `_executeCopyStage` when `hasActiveStages` is false. That is ~16 MB of idle VRAM at 1080p HDR (more at DPR 2) for the default effect-free WebGPU scene, which always routes through this pipeline for the canvas blit. Allocating the pair lazily on the first frame with an active stage (and dropping it when the chain empties) is the unowned fix.

items.title: Risk 7 / §6: _scenePipelineFormatGeneration is a manual contract between one writer and N readers; add a runtime colour-format check on cache hit; promote to a named export with a doc surface
items.claim: One missed reader = stale pipeline + format-mismatch warning.
items.evidence: Promoted: the contract is documented at WebGPUContext.ts:915-922 and exposed as the backend-agnostic `renderTargetGeneration` getter (:933-943; Context.js:818 returns 0), folded into Primitive's `needsCommands` and the five WebGPUPrimitiveCommands caches by Q14-HDR-TOGGLE-INVALIDATION (ROADMAP_AND_DEFERRED_WORK.md:694-710; probe-hdr-toggle-invalidation.mjs 284→0 errors). The central cache key now includes per-target colour formats and multisample state (Batch 825), so the CENTRAL cache cannot serve a stale-format pipeline. But the predicted failure mode still occurs in renderer-LOCAL caches: FIX_QUEUE §5 fleet3 row (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1203, CONFIRMED, lane A4 in flight) — 'generation change clears three pipeline caches but not `_materialPipelineCache`'; DEFERRED_WORK.md:9810 notes MSAA flips are only 'partially covered' and QUEUE_2026-07-15_CAMPAIGN9.md:124 `NEW-WEBGPU-SCENE-PASS-MSAA-FLIP-TRANSITION` is NOT STARTED. No runtime on-hit format check exists in WebGPURenderPipelineCache.ts (grep for sceneColorFormat empty); 31 files now read the counter.
items.surviving_record: ROADMAP_AND_DEFERRED_WORK.md Q14-HDR-TOGGLE-INVALIDATION (named getter); FIX_QUEUE §5 fleet3 row (WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1203, A4); QUEUE_2026-07-15_CAMPAIGN9.md NEW-WEBGPU-SCENE-PASS-MSAA-FLIP-TRANSITION
items.migrate_text: The scene-format epoch is now a named, documented surface — `WebGPUContext._scenePipelineFormatGeneration` (WebGPUContext.ts:915-922) behind the backend-agnostic `renderTargetGeneration` getter (:933-943; WebGL returns 0 at Context.js:818) — and the central pipeline cache key carries colour formats and sample count, so the central cache cannot hand back a stale-format pipeline. The manual half of the contract persists for the 31 renderer-local caches that must observe the counter themselves, and the predicted 'one missed reader' failure has materialised: `WebGPUGlobeSurfaceRenderer.ts:1203` clears three caches but not `_materialPipelineCache` (fleet3 row, lane A4), and MSAA flips remain only partially covered (`NEW-WEBGPU-SCENE-PASS-MSAA-FLIP-TRANSITION`, NOT STARTED). A structural guard — either registering every local cache with the epoch (the `WebGPUResourceCacheRegistry` pattern) or asserting the bound pipeline's target format against the scene FB on submit in debug builds — is still missing.

items.title: Risk 9: ContextRegistry is a single static on GraphicsContext._registry; two loaded cesium-engine modules (npm hoisting collision) break cross-context discovery
items.claim: Low probability, real.
items.evidence: GraphicsContext.ts:749 `private static _registry: ContextRegistry = new ContextRegistry();` with `register`/`unregister` at :833/:908; no `globalThis`/`Symbol.for` anchoring (grep empty). No DEFERRED_WORK, FIX_QUEUE, FAR (FAR-103 names ContextRegistry as a surface but for readiness, not module identity) or DX row names the duplicate-module case. ARCHITECTURE.md §2 describes the registry without the caveat. The 2026-09-02 review plan's ownership-lifetime lens covers 'context registry, ADR-3' and is the natural home.
items.migrate_text: `ContextRegistry` is still a per-module static (`GraphicsContext._registry`, packages/engine/Source/Renderer/GraphicsContext.ts:749, registered at :833 and unregistered at :908) with no `globalThis`/`Symbol.for` anchor, so an application that ends up with two copies of `@cesium/engine` (npm hoisting or duplicate bundling) gets two registries and split-screen / multi-view contexts cannot see each other. Low probability, but the multi-context guarantee in ARCHITECTURE.md §2 silently depends on single-module loading and nothing documents or detects the failure. No row owns it.

items.title: Model path sync pipeline compile on tileset stream hot path (incl. FOLLOW-UP C-P8-ASYNC)
items.claim: Per-model WebGPUModelPipelineCache with synchronous createRenderPipeline on every miss; caller hazard if async returns a Promise.
items.evidence: Landed: the on-screen model colour pipeline resolves through the central `WebGPURenderPipelineCache` async path behind a ready-gate (Batch 704 `87d15a8d13` C10-07-ASYNC-MODEL-PIPELINES; WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:84-92; WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5470-5479 passes `context.webgpuPipelineCache`), and immutable device resources are shared across models by generation (`acquireWebGPUModelDeviceResources`, C11-194, QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md:2187). Remaining by design: pick, velocity, classification, capture, silhouette and depth-write pipelines stay synchronous `device.createRenderPipeline` (WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:88-92; :979, :1065, :1136, :1372, :1463, :1521, :1591, :1650), and each model still instantiates its own cache object (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5470). Cold-start cost is measured and open as Q-134 (FIX_QUEUE_2026-08-27_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md:549: pipelines resolve at 1.6-2.6 s each, 12-15k cache misses before the first non-empty command list) and Q-143 frame-loop starvation (:457).
items.migrate_text: The model colour pipeline now compiles asynchronously behind a ready-gate (Batch 704; WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:84-92, WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5470-5479), but the pick, velocity, classification, capture, silhouette and depth-write variants remain synchronous `device.createRenderPipeline` calls by design (WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:979, :1065, :1136, :1372, :1463, :1521, :1591, :1650), and every model still owns a `WebGPUModelPipelineCache` instance (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5470) even though device-level resources are shared per generation (C11-194). The measured consequence is the open cold-start row Q-134 (FIX_QUEUE_2026-08-27_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md:549, 1.6-2.6 s per pipeline resolve, 12-15k misses before the first non-empty command list) and Q-143 streaming starvation.

What remains is uneven adoption by async completions: the Gaussian-splat renderer's pipeline promises land unguarded after the invalidation sweep (A5-1, FIX_QUEUE_2026-08-27_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md:50), the environment singletons have no ownership contract for in-flight work (S6-ENV-DETERMINISTIC-DESTROY-DEVICE-RECOVERY, DEFERRED_WORK.md:10721), and the ~1.7 s blind window before device.lost resolves is Q-49. The ownership-lifetime lens should audit which `createRenderPipelineAsync`/`mapAsync` continuations compare the generation on resume.

items.title: Canvas reconfigure race

items.evidence: WebGPUContext.ts:4655-4663 `resize()` -> `_applyCanvasConfig` -> WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts:96/:106/:122 `host._context.configure(...)`; none checks `_currentRenderPassEncoder`. Mitigation is call order: CesiumWidget.js:61/:69 resizes from the widget loop before `scene.render`, and no in-frame caller of `context.resize()` was found in Scene or Widget. No queue row.
items.migrate_text: `WebGPUContext.resize()` (packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU/WebGPUContext.ts:4655-4663) and the HDR/SDR fallback chain in WebGPUContextCanvasConfig.ts:96-122 call `context.configure()` with no guard against an open render pass or an acquired swap texture. Today this is safe only by call order — CesiumWidget.js:61/:69 resizes before `scene.render` and nothing resizes mid-frame — so the defect is latent. A one-line guard (defer the reconfigure to `endFrame` when `_currentRenderPassEncoder !== null` or `_currentTextureView` is held) would make the invariant explicit.

items.title: Failure mode: OOM - no pushErrorScope('out-of-memory'), no memory-pressure callback
items.claim: Only validation error scopes exist; a real OOM surfaces as device loss; no app-side graceful-degrade hook.
items.evidence: `grep pushErrorScope` over packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU finds 12 scopes, all `"validation"` (WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2271, WebGPUGlobeSurfaceShaders.ts:273/376, WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550/3676/3748/3819, WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:2125, WebGPUPrimitiveIndexUtils.ts:56, WebGPURenderBundleManager.ts:402); zero `out-of-memory` scopes; no `uncapturederror` listener. The per-frame allocation storm behind BUG-9 is addressed by WebGPURingBufferAllocator.ts (used by WebGPUContext.ts and WebGPUModelCameraArena.ts). FORK_ARCHITECTURE_REMEDIATION_PLAN_2026-07-13.md:205 states 'Runtime OOM or device loss enters recovery' as a principle but no queue row tracks OOM scoping or a memory-pressure callback.
items.migrate_text: The renderer never pushes an `out-of-memory` error scope: all 12 `pushErrorScope` sites under packages/engine/Source/Renderer/WebGPU are `"validation"` scopes (e.g. WebGPUSceneRenderer.ts:2271, WebGPUModelPipelineCache.ts:3550, WebGPUPostProcessPipeline.ts:2125) and no `uncapturederror` listener exists, so a texture or buffer allocation that fails for memory is only observed when it escalates to device loss and takes the WebGPUDeviceLossRecovery path. There is also no memory-pressure hook by which an application can degrade LOD or drop effects before that point. The FAR plan (:205) states the intent that runtime OOM enters recovery cleanly, but no row funds OOM-scoped allocation or a pressure callback.

A permanent `uncapturederror` handler that stamps the context id, plus an optional debug-mode per-pass scope, would close it cheaply.

items.title: Top-10 #10: `_scenePipelineFormatGeneration` invalidation contract is manual (23 files); no compile-time check that a new renderer reads it
items.claim: One missed reader = stale pipeline + format-mismatch validation warning.
items.evidence: Definition at WebGPUContext.ts:922 (`public _scenePipelineFormatGeneration = 0`, getter :942); 31 files under packages/engine/Source now reference it (up from 23). No `recompileForSceneFormat` method or `FormatAwareRenderer` interface exists (grep = 0). Same as N8. No queue row; FAR Phase 6 ('Complete generation invalidation/teardown', :302) is the nearest umbrella but names device generation, not the scene format generation.
items.migrate_text: The scene pipeline format contract is still convention-only: `WebGPUContext._scenePipelineFormatGeneration` (WebGPUContext.ts:922, getter :942) is read by 31 files, each of which must remember to compare its cached generation and rebuild, and nothing at compile time or lint time says which renderers are format-aware. A renderer that forgets keeps a pipeline whose color/depth format no longer matches the scene target after an HDR or MSAA change, and (per F7) the resulting validation error is not even caught after the first frame. Declaring a `recompileForSceneFormat(generation)` method on a shared interface that every feature renderer implements would make the contract greppable and compiler-checked.

No shipped Cesium path is known to depend on a masked clear, which is why it has never surfaced; the honest fix is a full-screen write-masked clear pipeline behind the ClearCommand path, and the finding should stay listed as a latent parity gap until a consumer appears.

items.title: WebGPU terrain-buffer lifetime is disconnected from Cesium's quadtree LRU/free lifecycle
items.claim: Terrain GPU buffers are keyed by coordinates only, retained with their CPU arrays, never released from GlobeSurfaceTile.freeResources, and evictStaleResources destroys inline before submit.
items.evidence: WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts:169-176 getTileKey is `${level}_${x}_${y}`; :577-588 evictStaleResources still calls vertexBuffer.destroy()/indexBuffer.destroy() inline (its host interface at :61 exposes only scheduleTextureDestroy, no buffer retirement); GlobeSurfaceTile.js:158-170 freeResources releases the water-mask texture only, no terrain-buffer lease; TileReplacementQueue.js:49 -> QuadtreeTile.js:611-620 still run before WebGPUContext.endFrame drains _pendingTextureDestroys (:3379). C11-34 (C9-15-TERRAIN-GPU-RESIDENCY-BUDGET / FAR-203) is NOT STARTED (QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md:1669, :2300, :2456); FAR-203 is 'planned' in the ledger (:253-256); DM-09/DM-10 call it 'adjacent'.
items.surviving_record: QUEUE_2026-07-18_CAMPAIGN11.md C11-34 (owner); FAR ledger FAR-203; QUEUE_2026-08-29_RESEARCH_DISPATCH.md DM-09/DM-10 (adjacent)
items.migrate_text: WebGPU terrain realizations live in WebGPUGlobeSurfaceTileBuffers.ts keyed by `${level}_${x}_${y}` (:169-176) with no payload revision, context or device generation in the key, and nothing on the quadtree free path releases them: GlobeSurfaceTile.js:158-170 freeResources drops only the water-mask texture, so TileReplacementQueue.trimTiles (:49) frees a tile's CPU side while its GPU buffers stay in _tileBufferCache. The only reclaim is evictStaleResources (:577-588), which destroys buffers inline; because Scene.render calls globe.endFrame before WebGPUContext.endFrame submits, any per-frame use of it can invalidate commands already recorded (the context's _pendingTextureDestroys batch at WebGPUContext.ts:553/:2932/:3379 is the right precedent and has no buffer counterpart). The Batch-731 API lane measured 2,102 buffers created / 561 destroyed over one flight (net +1,541) against WebGL's +5. Owner: C11-34 / FAR-203 (both unstarted); the fix shape is lease release from freeResources / mesh replacement / provider swap / device loss plus post-submit retirement, then a byte-budgeted zero-lease grace LRU - never a per-frame evictStaleResources(visibleTileKeys).

items.title: SceneOctree plane-mask results are compared with Intersect enum values
items.claim: The opt-in octree PVS compares a plane mask against Intersect.OUTSIDE/INSIDE and therefore never culls or short-circuits.

CullingVolume.js:196/205 returns MASK_OUTSIDE = 0xffffffff / MASK_INSIDE = 0 while Intersect.js:18 OUTSIDE = -1 (INSIDE = 1), so neither branch can ever match. The code is unchanged since a556f45724; Batches 1133/1149 (C11-62) touched only the dirty-revision rebuild; DEFERRED_WORK.md:10183 NEW-SCENEOCTREE-DIRTY-REVISION-REBUILD-AND-PVS-PROMOTION does not name the enum defect; no queue row does.
items.migrate_text: The opt-in SceneOctree (scene.renderScheduler.octree.enabled) cannot cull: OctreeNode.js:294-300 compares the result of CullingVolume.computeVisibilityWithPlaneMask - MASK_OUTSIDE 0xffffffff / MASK_INSIDE 0 (CullingVolume.js:196/205) - against Intersect.OUTSIDE (-1) and Intersect.INSIDE (1) at :300 and :322-325, so no subtree is ever rejected and the mask short-circuit never fires; the octree merely re-emits every command through a full traversal. items.evidence: Teardown half closed: WebGPUModelFeatureId.js:1433 destroyFeatureResourceGeneration, :1947 destroyUnboundRetiredFeaturePickGenerations, wired from WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:9073 (Batches 1072, 1195). Loss half: WebGPUContext.ts:7657 _clearAllCaches now drains a registered cache registry (_registerResourceCaches) and fires a WebGPUDeviceInvalidationBus; the model cache subscribes (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5314) and the culler pool/EDL do, but WebGPULabelRenderer.js and WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js contain no onDeviceInvalidated / device-generation guard (grep), so those per-collection _webgpuCache families still rely on their own scene-format invalidation only. items.surviving_record: Batches 1072/1195 (pick teardown); Batch 1199 (epoch resets); FIX_QUEUE_2026-08-27_AUDIT_FINDINGS.md Q-86
items.migrate_text: Device-loss recovery now runs through a registered cache registry (WebGPUContext.ts:7657 _clearAllCaches, _registerResourceCaches) and a WebGPUDeviceInvalidationBus that the model renderer (WebGPUModelRenderer.ts:5314), culler pool and EDL subscribe to, but the label and polyline collection caches (WebGPULabelRenderer.js:838-871, WebGPUPolylineRenderer.js:1596) subscribe to nothing and carry no device-generation check, so after a recovery they can present old-device pipelines and buffers until a scene-format bump happens to clear them. items.title: OIT composite bind group is rebuilt and its derived-pipeline key is insufficiently specific
items.claim: WebGPUOIT rebuilds the composite bind group every composite and keys derived pipelines by shader length.
items.evidence: WebGPUOIT.ts:259 executeComposite calls _updateCompositeBindGroup() unconditionally and :350-372 createBindGroup()s a fresh 'OIT-Composite-BindGroup' each call; :706 `cacheKey = `${shaderCode.length}_${fragEntry}_${config.label ?? ""}`` (own comment at :381: 'keyed by shader-code length'). OIT is contained default-off under FAR-003 (CesiumDebug.webgpuOIT); FAR-404/FAR-704 (ledger :429-434, :586-594) cover the MSAA topology and dual-source experiment, not this key/reuse defect; DEFERRED_WORK.md:10389-10429 records the flip-evidence gates without it.
items.migrate_text: Before OIT can leave FAR-003 containment its cache identity must be fixed: WebGPUOIT.ts:259 rebuilds the composite bind group on every executeComposite (:350-372 allocates a new GPUBindGroup each frame although the accumulation/revealage views only change on resize or device loss), and derived OIT pipelines are keyed at :706 by shader-code length, fragment entry and label, so two distinct shaders of equal length with the same label alias. Fix: rebuild the composite bind group only when its views change, and key derived pipelines by module identity (the WeakMap-backed webgpuObjectIdentity the central caches use) plus target format, sample count and depth state, then re-run the intersecting-translucency, resize, MSAA, format and device-loss gates. FIX LATER (feature stays reachable, default-off).
